name: correctness

findings.message: The pre-scan concludes 'all complete = all from prior iter' even when some members completed in the current interrupted iteration, causing build to be re-dispatched with stage.start when it should be skipped (DSCMBR-1 violated).
findings.quote:
if [[ "$_cid_nc" -eq 0 ]]; then
            # All complete from prior iter; run all members fresh, emit stage.start for first.
            _resume_first_iter=false
            _from_stage_start=true
        fi

findings.message: The DSCMBR-1 test sets `stage_statuses.test = "aborted"` rather than `"complete"`, so the pre-scan's 'all complete' path (which fires when test has status "complete" from iter N-1 and build already completed in iter N) is never exercised; a future regression in that edge case would stay green.

`skip_until_stage` is set to `from_stage` before the dispatch loop, and both cycle:* and stage:* arms clear it only when the matching unit is found; if `--from-stage` names a cycle, the stage:* arm at line 3977 would never see `_ust == skip_until_stage` (stage names ≠ cycle IDs), so `skip_until_stage` is never cleared by the stage:* path and the cycle's own clearing at line 3653 is the only exit — this works, but after the cycle the resume skip guard (`$resume_mode && [[ -z "$skip_until_stage" ]]`) activates for all subsequent leaf stages, potentially skipping stages that the user intended to run after the targeted cycle when those stages happen to be marked complete.

The cycle-member artifact check inside the resume skip guard uses `"${_cyc_id//-/_}"` to build the `_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_*` var name, while the outer sanitisation for the jq key uses `"${_cyc_id//[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/}"` — two different transformations applied to the same `_cyc_id` within a few lines; a cycle ID with characters beyond `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` would look up the wrong var, missing member stages and silently skipping the artifact check.

The temporary `resume_mode=true` override used to skip persona preflight for `--from-stage` is applied before the auto-resume block; if the auto-resume block later resets `resume_mode=false` (e.g., because the state file reports `complete`), the final `--from-stage` validity check at line 2313 fires with `resume_mode=false` and rejects the run with a misleading message ('--from-stage is only valid with --resume') even though the user passed `--resume` explicitly.

reason: the correctness lens found a medium or high or critical problem the change introduced
